sentences.text: Razanandrongobe was a carnivorous ziphosuchian crocodyliform that inhabited Madagascar during the Middle Jurassic period.
The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — consists of a right maxilla fragment measuring 192 mm long, 124 mm high, and 96 mm wide, forming part of a highly specialized skull.
This skull featured a robust, rounded U-shaped snout that stood taller than it was wide.
Uniquely, the very tip of the lower jaw was toothless, spanning a width equal to the diameter of more than one tooth.
At 7 meters in length, Razanandrongobe was the largest known terrestrial Mesoeucrocodylia from the Jurassic and the largest Notosuchian overall.
Its massive size suggests it likely occupied a predatory niche similar to that of theropod dinosaurs.
The initial fossils, including a maxilla fragment and teeth, were found in the Bathonian-aged Sakaraha Formation near Mahajanga, Madagascar.
Giovanni Pasini first verified the presence of fossil-bearing strata in the region in October 2001.
A privately funded expedition by teams from the Milan Natural History Museum and the Civic Museum of Fossils of Besano was launched in April 2003.
Additional specimens, including skull fragments and a tooth crown, were described in 2017 by Dal Sasso, Pasini, Maganuco, and Guillaume Fleury.
The skull anatomy supports the inference that Razanandrongobe's diet included hard tissues such as bones and tendons.
Wear patterns on the teeth suggest the animal bit into bones or other hard objects, causing enamel to chip similarly to observations in tyrannosaurs.
The denticles on the teeth were adapted to break bones, based on their size, shape, and the presence of a rounded depression at the base between neighboring denticles.
The teeth bore large serrations on both front and rear edges that were proportionally larger than those of Tyrannosaurus.
In 2017, Dal Sasso and colleagues suggested that feeding adaptations, combined with its large skull and body size, would have made Razanandrongobe a highly specialized terrestrial predator.
The environment where Razanandrongobe lived is inferred to have been river-based or lake-based.
Razanandrongobe was a carnivorous ziphosuchian crocodyliform that lived in Madagascar during the Middle Jurassic.
Razanandrongobe is classified within the family Sebecosuchia.
Razanandrongobe belongs to the parent group Baurusuchia.
In 2024, Razanandrongobe was recovered as a non-baurusuchid baurusuchian.
In 2017, Dal Sasso and colleagues refined the phylogenetic placement of Razanandrongobe following the discovery of additional specimens.
Razanandrongobe fossils date to the Bathonian stage of the Middle Jurassic, between 167.7 and 164.7 million years ago.
Razanandrongobe is the oldest known representative of the Notosuchia group.
Razanandrongobe predates all other known Notosuchians by 42 million years, partially filling a ghost lineage.
Razanandrongobe lived 42 million years before the oldest known notosuchians.
Researchers inferred a total length of 7 meters, a hip height of 1.6 meters, and a weight of 800 to 1000 kilograms based on comparisons with baurusuchids.
Maganuco and colleagues debated whether unfused interdental plates were a synapomorphy of Archosauriformes or a plesiomorphic characteristic of crocodyliforms, theropods, and poposaurids.
The original material of Razanandrongobe was considered too fragmentary for phylogenetic analysis of archosauriforms because it lacked nearly all characteristics used in such analyses.
The close relationship between Razanandrongobe and the younger lineage Sebecosuchia is considered provisional by researchers.
